title: refactor: unwind the retired striped/bordered/virtualScroll list-view surface (objectstack#7176)
body:
Fixes #4649

Pre-bump adaptation **1 of 2** for #4636 / PR #4639: it lands on the current `main`
(the `@objectstack/spec@17.0.0-rc.6` pin) and is behaviour-neutral there, so the GA
bump does not have to carry it.

## What was measured before anything was removed

objectstack#7176 (maintainer-ruled 2026-08-10) retired `list.striped`,
`list.bordered` and `list.virtualScroll` as pass-through-only. That premise was
re-verified on this branch rather than taken on trust, and the decisive fact is
the terminal one: **`packages/plugin-grid` — the `object-grid` renderer every
one of these relays feeds — contains zero references to `striped`, `bordered` or
`virtualScroll`.** No renderer anywhere in the repo applies them either; the only
`striped` / `bordered` reads that exist belong to different, live components
(`page:card`'s `bordered`, which `containers.tsx` really does apply, and
`plugin-detail`'s `virtualScroll` options object) and are untouched here.

So the chain carried values into a component that never read them, and removing
it changes no rendered output.

## Files that came off the chain

| Package | File | What went |
|---|---|---|
| `@object-ui/react` | `src/spec-bridge/bridges/list-view.ts` | the three spec-to-node relay lines |
| `@object-ui/plugin-list` | `src/ListView.tsx` | `striped` / `bordered` in `baseProps`, `virtualScroll` in the grid branch |
| `@object-ui/plugin-view` | `src/ObjectView.tsx` | all three relay sites — `generateViewSchema`, the table-schema memo, and the ListView props block |
| `@object-ui/app-shell` | `src/views/ObjectView.tsx` | the `viewDef ?? listSchema` relays (the region the card cited as ~1766-1838; re-derived, it matched) |
| `@object-ui/types` | `src/objectql.ts` | `ObjectGridSchema.striped` / `.bordered` / `.virtualScroll`, `NamedListView.striped` / `.bordered` / `.virtualScroll` |
| `@object-ui/types` | `src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` | `ObjectGridSchema`'s `striped` / `bordered` |
| `@object-ui/components` | `metadata/ObjectGrid.component.yml` | the `striped` / `bordered` prop declarations |
| `@object-ui/app-shell` | `src/views/metadata-admin/previews/block-config.ts` | the page-block inspector's `striped` / `bordered` toggles, plus their two label keys in `metadata-admin/i18n.ts` (en + zh) |

The inspector entry is the one addition to the card's enumerated file surface. It
is the same declaration in its most user-facing form — a designer toggle writing
a key that no schema declares and no renderer reads — and that file's own rule is
"keep each field `name` aligned with the property name the corresponding renderer
reads". Leaving it would have kept an authoring surface alive for keys this PR
removes everywhere else. It is not claimed by any sibling card (#4650 holds
`metadata-admin/widgets.tsx`, a different file, untouched here).

## What deliberately did NOT change

`ListViewSchema` in `types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` keeps importing the spec's
list-view fields **by reference**, so on the rc.6 pin the three still ride in.
That is the point, and the comment added there says so: on the GA bump the same
import carries the spec's `retiredKey()` tombstones, and an author writing one
gets a protocol-level rejection. Adding the keys to `LIST_VIEW_LOCAL_OVERRIDES`
to "finish the cleanup" would do the opposite — it drops the tombstone and hands
the key back to `BaseSchema`'s passthrough, turning a loud rejection into a
silently accepted dead key.

## Tests

Fixture triage, not a batch re-spell:

- **`types/p1-spec-alignment.test.ts`** — the `virtualScroll` acceptance case (the
  row that fails TS2322 on PR #4639's branch) is replaced by a retirement pin, and
  a second pin covers `striped` / `bordered` on `NamedListView`. Both are green on
  rc.6 **and** GA, because they assert against objectui's own types, which no pin
  moves.
- The ObjectGrid pin asserts the **zod** shape, not the interface. The
  `@ts-expect-error` written first failed as TS2578 "unused directive": every
  interface in that family extends `BaseSchema`, which carries
  `[key: string]: any`, so none of them can reject an excess key. `NamedListView`
  is a plain interface and does reject, so it keeps the type-level form.
- **`react/P1SpecBridge.test.ts`** — the two `pass through` cases become one case
  that feeds the retired keys in and asserts the bridge drops them, with a
  surviving neighbour (`resizable`) proving the fixture reached the bridge at all.
  It compiles on both pins because `transformListView(spec: any)` types its input
  as `any`.
- **`plugin-list/ListView.test.tsx`** — the two forwarding cases are removed, not
  re-spelled: both only asserted `container` was truthy, so they were green whether
  or not the key was forwarded, which is how a dead pass-through sat here unread.
- **`types/phase2-schemas.test.ts`** — `striped` / `bordered` trimmed from the
  `ListViewSchema` fixture. This is a **GA breaker the card did not name**: the
  fixture parses against the spec-derived schema, so it would have gone red on the
  bump.
- **`plugin-view/ObjectView.test.tsx`** — the live-preview fixture is re-spelled to
  `rowHeight` / `color`, keeping it a real appearance change.

## Verification

Every run below was taken at HEAD `68fb51692` — the final commit, after the
review-visible edits, not before them. All from the repo root, per AGENTS.md.

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ packages/react/ packages/plugin-list/ \
                     packages/plugin-view/ packages/components/
  Test Files  256 passed (256)
       Tests  2763 passed (2763)

pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/
  Test Files  396 passed (396)
       Tests  3738 passed | 1 skipped (3739)

pnpm --filter ...(the six touched packages) type-check     all Done
pnpm --filter ...(the six touched packages) lint           0 errors (2392 pre-existing warnings)

check:control-bytes      OK (4181 tracked text files)
check:spec-symbols       OK (1252 files vs 4834 spec export names)
check:i18n-keys          OK (every call-site key resolves against the en pack)
check:i18n-drift         OK (no en value changed in this range)
check:phantom-deps       OK
changeset presence / no-major   OK (1 changeset, minor)
```

The app-shell suite is quoted because it earned it: its **first** pass over this
change was red — 4 tests in 2 files — and the failure was mine. Removing the two
inspector fields broke `PageBlockInspector.i18n.test.tsx` and the
`block-config-i18n` en-label sample, both of which were using
`object-grid.striped` / `.bordered` as their `boolean`-kind coverage. Deleting
the assertions would have silently dropped that branch from the suite, so the
coverage moved to `page:card.bordered` instead — same field kind, and a prop
`containers.tsx` actually applies, so the case can no longer be satisfied by a
field nothing reads.
